newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen higher on carry-over, peso firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen higher on carry-over, peso firm.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen up on momentum, Dow
--Peso likely firm on strong U.S. long bond
--Cetes overnight rate viewed down on FOMC, peso
Traders and analysts saw stocks opening with upside potential on Thursday on follow-through and an expected firm start on Wall Street
"I think the party will continue. It should take a breather (sometime), but foreigners are still buying," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage.
Technical analysts situated resistance at 4,580 points on the IPC index, which closed at a record 4,559.23 on Wednesday.

Traders expected the peso to recover from Wednesday's weakness on favorable reaction in the U.S. bond market to non-farm payrolls data released early Thursday. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 33/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9400/7.9600 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9470/7.9650 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.9620/7.9650.

Overnight rates on Cetes were seen easing down from Wednesday's close of 19.90 percent after the Federal Open Market Committee decided not to raise U.S. interest rates, and due to forecast firmness on the peso, dealers said.
